items.title: 52263_Sonny Greer oral history interview
items.q: this Miss Krueger, every time she saw me I had a cap on or just a pair of pants or old shirt or something, caddy ing, she had never seen me dressed up.

ctx.x: I'm the only soul brother in between all them days. so now we get a gig. We start playing the basketball games and the local dances, all that stuff, but I'm still 15 years old. I couldn't go on a gig in Newark, New Jersey or East Orange, or places like that, big affairs. We had a manager of the band, him and his wife, because we were all kids, they used to chaperone us, you know.

So now we get this gig, at the same golf club, the Deer Country Club, a big affair, so now I get all sharp. My mother keep me sharp because I was only colored around there, keep me sharp. I was all dressed up in my blue suit, my finery, so we go to this Deer Country Club. I had never been in the clubhouse in my life, only on the golf course, but in the meantime, this Miss Krueger, every time she saw me I had a cap on or just a pair of pants or old shirt or something, caddy ing, she had never seen me dressed up.

So now -- I forgot all about her, we're playing this Deer Country Club, all the white boys and me and we had a thing we did -- well, we had one white girl, sang. We used to sing by theirself. I'd sing by myself, and then a couple of them would sing and we had a trio -- two white boys, a white boy, the girl and me. Got up to sing. So now the people coming in to the dance and right on the ringside is this broad, this Miss Krueger. Big party.
